newsitem.title: USA: OCAW appeals NLRB dismissal of Crown labor charges.
newsitem.headline: OCAW appeals NLRB dismissal of Crown labor charges.

text.p: Union workers locked out for over a year at Crown Central Petroleum Corp's Pasadena, Texas, refinery appealed a decision by a National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) regional Texas office dismissing union charges of unfair labor practices against Crown.
The Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers International Union (OCAW) said Thursday it sent the appeal on June 2 to the NLRB's general counsel in Washington D.C.
The NLRB regional office in Dallas/Forth Worth dismissed the charges in April and refused to issue a complaint against Crown.
"We had relatively low expectations on the regional level but we are more confident the Office of the General Counsel will appeal the dismissal," said OCAW representative Richard Miller.
Lawyers for Crown could not immediately be reached.
The charges, stemming from a lockout that began in February last year, includes issues of bargaining in good faith, subcontracting work and union member requests for 401(k) plan withdrawals.
Miller said the company wants to eliminate or subcontract about 89 of the 251 union jobs at the refinery.
Crown officials have said the number of jobs it plans to cut is now just 60 given retirements and resignations of workers since the lockout began.
Since the lockout, the two sides have met about six times, most recently in November in talks that quickly broke down, said Miller.
